chunks: 603 – And it is narrated from Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام that he said:

I asked my father, Sayyid al-ʿĀbidīn عليه السلام, and said to him: O my father, inform me about our grandfather, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, when he was taken up to the heaven and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him with fifty prayers—how was it that he did not ask Him for a reduction on behalf of his Ummah until Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام said to him: Return to your Lord and ask Him for a reduction, for your Ummah cannot bear that?

He said: O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله does not make proposals to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, nor does he review with Him anything that He commands him. So when Mūsā عليه السلام asked him that, and became an intercessor to Him on behalf of his Ummah, it was not permissible for him to reject the intercession of his brother Mūsā عليه السلام. Thus he returned to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and asked Him for a reduction until He returned them to five prayers.

He said: So I said to him: O my father, then why did he not return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and not ask Him for a reduction from five prayers, while Mūsā عليه السلام had asked him to return to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and ask Him for a reduction? He said: O my son, he عليه السلام intended to obtain lightening for his Ummah together with the reward of fifty prayers, due to the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten times its like."

Do you not see that when he عليه السلام descended to the earth, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came down to him and said: O Muḥammad, indeed your Lord sends you salām and says to you: Indeed, they are five with fifty.
"The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants."

He said: So I said to him: O my father, is it not that Allah, majestic is His mention, is not described by place? He said: Yes, Allah is exalted above that in great exaltation. I said: Then what is the meaning of the statement of Mūsā عليه السلام to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, Return to your Lord? He said: Its meaning is the meaning of the statement of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:
"Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."
And the meaning of the statement of Mūsā عليه السلام:
"And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased."
And the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic:

Meaning: perform hajj to the House of Allah. O my son, indeed the Kaʿbah is the House of Allah, so whoever performs hajj to the House of Allah has indeed intended Allah. And the mosques are the houses of Allah, so whoever strives toward them has indeed striven toward Allah and intended Him. And the one praying, so long as he is in his salat, is standing before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has regions in His heavens, and whoever is taken up to a region from them has indeed been taken up to Him. Do you not hear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying:
"The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him."
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in the story of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليهما السلام:
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
"To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed—He raises it."

key_terms.التَّخْفِيفَ: reduction or lightening of the burden of the prescribed prayers
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the House of Allah, toward which hajj signifies intending Allah
key_terms.الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ: good words that ascend to Allah
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدَ: the houses of Allah, toward which striving signifies seeking Him
key_terms.بِمَكَانٍ: a place or location, negated here from Allah’s description
key_terms.خَمْسِ صَلَوَاتٍ: the final daily obligatory prayers, retaining the reward of fifty
key_terms.خَمْسِينَ صَلَاةً: the original prescription of fifty prayers in the Miʿrāj account
key_terms.شَفِيعًا: an intercessor pleading on behalf of the Ummah

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله accept the reduction of fifty prayers to five, and what does ‘return to your Lord’ mean if Allah is not in a place?
ai.summary: This hadith explains why the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله did not initially ask for a reduction in the prescribed prayers, emphasizing his perfect submission to the divine command and the accepted intercession of Mūsā عليه السلام. It also clarifies that references to returning or ascending to Allah do not imply place or location for Him, but indicate turning toward Him through His appointed sanctities, worship, and nearness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.603 – It is narrated from Zaid ibn Ali ibn al-Hussain (as) who said:

"I asked my father, the Master of the Worshippers (Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain (as)), saying,
'O’ my father, inform me about our grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (sw), when he was taken up to the heavens and his Lord (azj) commanded him with fifty prayers. Why did he not ask for a reduction for his community until Musa (as) said to him, "Return to your Lord (azj) and ask for a reduction, for your community will not be able to bear this"?'

Imam Ali ibn Al-Hussain (as) said: 'O’ my son, the Messenger of Allah (sw) does not propose or make demands from his Lord (azj), nor does he dispute any command He gives him. However, when Musa (as) suggested it and became an intercessor on behalf of his community, it was not appropriate for him to refuse the intercession of his brother Musa. So he returned to his Lord (azj) and asked for a reduction until it was reduced to five prayers.'

I then said: 'O’ my father, why did he not return to his Lord (azj) and ask for a reduction from five prayers, even though Musa had suggested that?'
Imam (as) said: 'O’ my son, The Prophet (sw) wished to ensure a lightening of the burden while preserving the reward of fifty prayers for his community, as Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says,
"Whoever brings a good deed shall have ten times its like" (Suran Al-An’am 6:160).

Do you not see that when he returned to the earth, Archangel Jibril (as) descended to him and said: "O’ Muhammad, your Lord (azj) sends you greetings and says: Indeed, they are five (prayers) equating to fifty (in reward).
No word is changed with Me, and I am not unjust to My servants."'

I said: 'O’ my father, is not Allah (swt), the Glorified, beyond being confined to a place?'
Imam (as) said: 'Yes, Allah (swt) is far above such limitations.'
I then asked: 'So what is the meaning of Musa’s statement to the Messenger of Allah (sw), "Return to your Lord (azj)"?'
Imam (as) said: 'It means the same as Ibrahim’s statement (as):
"Indeed, I will go to my Lord (azj); He will guide me" (Surah As-Saffat 37:99),
"I hastened to You, my Lord (azj), so that You might be pleased" (Surah Taha 20:84),

which means pilgrimage to the House of Allah (swt).
O’ my son, the Kaaba is the House of Allah (swt), and whoever performs Hajj to the House of Allah (swt) has sought Allah (swt). The mosques are the Houses of Allah (swt), so whoever strives toward them strives toward Allah (swt) and intends Him.
While praying, one is standing in the presence of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. Verily, Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, has realms in His heavens, and whoever is taken up to one of these realms is taken up to Him.
Do you not hear Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, say:
"The angels and the spirit ascend to Him" (Surah Al-Ma’arij 70:4)
and in the story of Isa (Jesus (as)):
"But Allah (swt) raised him to Himself" (Surah An-Nisa 4:158),
"To Him ascend good words, and He raises righteous deeds" (Surah Fatir 35:10).'
